To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the sphere formation assay is an efficient tool for the enrichment and isolation of equine EpSCs from skin and that this technique can be successfully applied to eliminate contaminating cell types.
sphere formation is a valuable tool to isolate and purify epithelial-like stem cells from equine skin.

(i) EpSCs are able to form spheres, (ii) the sphere forming efficiency is significantly higher in EpSC medium than in differentiation medium, (iii) the sphere forming capacity increases over time, (iv) sphere forming capacity increases at subsequent passaging, (v) a keratinocyte contamination can be purified by seeding at ultralow densities in suspension and (vi) sphere formation is a promising strategy for the purification of EpSCs from primary skin samples.

the development of a novel and simple method to isolate and enrich EpSCs for the treatment of skin diseases in horses.
the development of a reliable and reproducible method to isolate and purify EpSC cultures from equine skin.
the isolation, purification, and characterization of equine EpSCs, which may serve as a valuable tool in the treatment of skin disorders in the horse.
